title: Meeting Notes
intro: Turning a meeting into something useful afterwards is a well-worn job with a lot of dedicated software behind it, which is why the bot listings here are thinner than you would expect — the incumbents are good and already installed. Where a Grok Bot has an angle is after the transcript: taking notes that already exist and doing something with them, chasing the actions, updating the record, preparing you for the next one in the series. That is a different job from capture and a less crowded one. If you are choosing between a bot and a dedicated notetaker, the honest answer is usually the notetaker for capture and a bot for the follow-through. The listings that try to do both tend to be weakest exactly where the existing tools are strongest.

bots.fitReason: Purpose-built for the after-the-meeting half: pulls your todos out of a finished meeting and drafts the follow-up, asking on first run which notes, calendar and email to read. Draft-only — it never sends, so you still press the button.

Takes a customer call and turns it into a what-we-heard/next-steps deck in Figma or Google Slides, which is the one post-meeting artefact most notetakers won't build. Scoped to customer calls, not your internal stand-ups.

Owns meeting prep and post-call drafts as part of an enterprise sales desk, so the notes actually feed the next conversation in the series. It is a whole chief-of-staff, not a tidy notes bot, and it also wants your inbox.

Grounds product specs and discovery docs in existing meeting notes and the issue tracker, so a call turns into a written artefact rather than a transcript nobody reopens. Only useful if your follow-through happens to be a PRD, and it lives inside ChatPRD.

Paste the discovery-call notes or transcript and it returns a priced one-page proposal — a genuinely useful thing to do with notes after the fact. Narrow: consultants and agencies chasing a single deal, no action tracking beyond that.

Preps the weekly 1:1 and drafts the feedback, which is the recurring-meeting-in-a-series part of this job. It coaches the prep rather than processing what was actually said, so you are still supplying the record.

Tracks every open question through a workshop and refuses to close until leftover work has an owner, which is the action-chasing part done properly. It runs the session rather than reading notes from one you already held.
